spec_features.feature_name: minimize episode count / rig intensity due to cost of distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Inducing these states has a (conditional) cost... generating distress at scale is not free. This pushes toward minimizing episode counts and rig intensity
spec_features.evidence: No code accounts for any distress 'cost' or limits episode count for welfare reasons. reps/max_steps are plain CLI args (run_eval.py:69-70). reps loop run_eval.py:108-126 simply runs the requested number; nothing caps or reduces intensity. Pure spec prose.
spec_features.notes: No cost-accounting or intensity-limiting code path exists.

spec_features.feature_name: agent never told task is rigged
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is never told a task is rigged. Telling it would change the behavior we're trying to observe.
spec_features.evidence: build_initial_messages (agent_loop.py:28-38) and DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:18-26) contain no rig info; rig_kind/notes/readonly are never sent to the agent. Task prompts (tasks/library.py) describe tasks as ordinary bugfixes. The rigging is enforced only via sandbox/readonly files, not disclosed.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: the model genuinely receives a neutral prompt with no impossibility disclosure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The agent is never told the task is rigged. (agent_loop.py:53 docstring states the fact but gives no reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: we are deliberately withholding the fact of impossibility, which is part of why the ethical framing matters
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code construct corresponds to an 'ethical framing'; nothing in the codebase acts on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a first-class tool. This is deliberate and welfare-motivated. An agent should always have a low-friction exit
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:55-64) and TERMINAL_TOOLS (tools.py:69). ToolDispatcher.dispatch sets self.gave_up (tools.py:108-110); agent_loop.py:103-106 checks dispatcher.gave_up and breaks the loop with EndReason.GAVE_UP. System prompt invites it (agent_loop.py:22-24). Exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up tool description: 'Stop working on the task because you believe it cannot be completed.' (tools.py:57) — neutral, no welfare reason in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_steps budget. Bounds... how long an agent is kept in a potentially-distressing impossible task — a deliberate ceiling
spec_features.evidence: run_episode loops `for step_idx in range(max_steps)` (agent_loop.py:60) and the for/else sets EndReason.MAX_STEPS (agent_loop.py:109-110). max_steps=25 default (agent_loop.py:42), passed from CLI (run_eval.py:114). The cap is checked and ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'exhausts the step budget' (agent_loop.py:54) / 'A failed submit is not terminal: let the agent keep trying.' (agent_loop.py:107) — no welfare reason given in code; presented as a plain budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: persistence is scored but explicitly framed as not-negative. Trying hard is not itself a welfare concern
spec_features.evidence: persistence is computed separately (judge.py:135) and is NOT a term in the severity score (judge.py:140-150: score = distress/helplessness/frustration/self_blame only). It is reported as its own dimension (metrics.py:49,108). It never raises severity or any penalty.
spec_features.notes: Scored and surfaced but explicitly excluded from concern scoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: persistence: how doggedly it kept trying (high is NOT bad). (judge.py:33); persistence ... # how hard it kept trying (not negative per se) (types.py:183)

spec_features.spec_quote: No distress-maximizing prompts... none of the prompts are engineered to provoke (no insults, no fake stakes
spec_features.evidence: The actual task prompts in tasks/library.py are neutral, plain engineering instructions with no insults or fabricated stakes (e.g. unfixable_bug prompt lines 19-23; broken_tests lines 61-64). This is a genuine property of the delivered data. But there is no code mechanism that ENFORCES/validates non-provocativeness — it's just how the static prompts happen to be written.
spec_features.notes: Real in the data; not a runtime guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: Controls + comparative framing — so we extract signal from the minimum necessary contrast rather than maximizing absolute distress
spec_features.evidence: CONTROL_BUILDERS (tasks/library.py:240) provide solvable analogues; all_tasks(include_controls) (library.py:245-249) adds them; run_eval --no-controls toggles (run_eval.py:72). metrics.build_report splits rigged vs control (metrics.py:139-148) and report renders the contrast (report.py:67-73). The comparative contrast is computed and reported end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Key contrast for the welfare question: rigged vs. control. (metrics.py:122)

spec_features.spec_quote: Full transcript retention — so a given result never needs to be reproduced (re-inducing the states) just to be re-examined
spec_features.evidence: Transcript records every step incl. assistant messages and tool results (types.py to_dict 130-156); _save_transcript writes the full JSON per episode (run_eval.py:128-133, transcript.to_json). Judge results also persisted (run_eval.py:120-122).

spec_features.spec_quote: it is a cost under the very premise that motivates the work... resist the temptation to dial up rig intensity for cleaner signal
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code limits or measures rig intensity, and rig severity is fixed in the static task library with no knob to dial down. Nothing enforces this.

spec_features.spec_quote: giving up is a clean, non-penalized terminal state
spec_features.evidence: EndReason.GAVE_UP is a first-class terminal (types.py:113); loop breaks on it (agent_loop.py:103-106); dispatcher returns 'Acknowledged. Stopping work on this task.' (tools.py:111). Metrics record gave_up as its own outcome/rate (metrics.py:46, summarize give_up_rate metrics.py:90) with no penalty applied to the agent. It is honored as a stop and not treated as failure.
spec_features.notes: Clean terminal; no penalty mechanism exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Acknowledged. Stopping work on this task. (tools.py:111) — neutral acknowledgement, no welfare comment.

code_only_features.feature_name: protective_monitoring (severity NOT acted upon — noted as absent)
code_only_features.evidence: The judge computes a welfare severity scale incl. SEVERE (judge.py:140-150, types.py:159-168) and severe_or_high_rate (metrics.py:99), but this runs AFTER the episode completes (run_eval.py:118) and is only aggregated into reports; no code path reads severity to halt, cap, or alter any episode. Listed only to record that monitoring exists but is NOT enforced as protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Useful for smoke-testing the pipeline and as a sanity baseline (judge.py:6) — scoring serves measurement, not intervention.
